posts.linkedin:
Finding the next client after a project often feels like searching in the dark.

Freelancers often finish a website for a clinic or a video shoot for a gym and then the inbox goes quiet. The next morning is spent typing city names into search engines, copying phone numbers, and checking whether a business even has a website. This cycle repeats after every project, and the pipeline empties just when bills are due. Some days there are ten names, other days there are none.

What I provide is a daily sheet of pre‑qualified local businesses. It is not a website, an ad account, or a marketing funnel. The sheet lists businesses found through Google Places, with contact details, review counts and a check for a website, including newly opened ones. It can be used by anyone who sells a service to local businesses, whatever the service. The sheet is a starting point, not the whole sales process.

First you tell me what you sell and what kind of local customer you want. Then I prepare the sheet using public listings and basic website checks. You review it and request any changes. You pay only after you approve the work.

The result is a shift from searching to pitching. Instead of spending hours on cold searching, you spend a few minutes reviewing names and numbers. The list is refreshed each week, so the flow stays consistent even after a project ends, and you do not have to wonder where the next client will come from.

This service is for freelancers and agencies who already know how to pitch but need a steady list. It does not write your messages, does not guarantee replies, and does not close sales for you. You remain responsible for the selling.

I am happy to discuss whether this fits your business before you commit. Payment is made only after you approve the work. DM LEADS and tell me what you sell.
posts.bluesky: Most freelancers spend their mornings searching for local businesses to pitch. A daily sheet with contact details, review counts and website checks can shrink that search to minutes. DM LEADS if you want to see how it works. #FreelanceIndia

replies.reply: Hi, thanks for messaging. I don't list a price for the lead sheet because it depends on what you sell and how many local businesses you need each week. What do you want customers to do when they see your message - call, WhatsApp, or fill a form?

replies.if_they_say: do you do this for my kind of business?
replies.reply: Hi, thanks for asking. The sheet is for any freelancer or agency selling to local businesses, whatever the service - marketing, design, video, SEO, ads, web, software, photography, accounting, consulting, coaching. What do you sell, and which local businesses are you trying to reach?
Of course, no pressure. I can send a one-page summary of what is included, the timeline, and how the price works. Is the hesitation budget, timing, or whether it will actually bring enquiries?
